meta_title: Topmindspace — open-source tools for streams, notes, writing, and slides
meta_description: Open-source projects from Topmindspace: Topmind, a personal stream and knowledge workspace (desktop app, Obsidian plugin, skill pack), writing skills, and a presentation skill that builds pageable HTML and editable PPTX.
og_title: Topmindspace — open-source tools for streams, notes, writing, and slides
og_description: Topmind stream and knowledge workspace (desktop app, Obsidian plugin, skill pack), plus writing and presentation skills. Files stay in local Markdown.
footer_verified: Versions checked on 2026-10-13. Each repository's Releases page is the source of truth.
footer_tagline: Open-source tools built around local Markdown.
hero_lede: Five open-source projects for a personal stream, knowledge management, writing, and presentations. Notes, articles, and slides are files on your own disk, and changes proposed by AI are written only after you confirm.
know_lead: Notes, clips, and documents land on a timeline as Markdown in your workspace. Organizing and todos are proposed first and written only after you confirm. The desktop app, the Obsidian plugin, and the skill pack share one workspace convention, so switching between them needs no migration.
desk_what: A three-column desktop workbench: a stream timeline plus an AI workspace with Chat, Suggestions, Todos, and Apps tabs. The interface is available in Simplified Chinese and English.
desk_for: People who want a standalone app and a visual place to confirm AI suggestions.
desk_note: Homebrew install for macOS (Apple silicon). Windows and Linux builds (.exe, .AppImage, .deb) are on Releases.
desk_shot_suggest: Suggestions tab: organizing and todos wait for your confirmation
desk_shot_suggest_alt: Topmind suggestions panel with items waiting for confirmation
desk_shot_ingest: Document ingest: drop a file, get Markdown
desk_shot_ingest_alt: Topmind knowledge ingest: drop files to convert them to Markdown
obs_what: Opens the stream in Obsidian’s main area. The right sidebar AI panel has Chat, Suggestions, Todos, and History tabs. Changes proposed by AI are written after you confirm, and notes stay as Markdown in your vault.
obs_for: People already on Obsidian who want the stream inside their vault. Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later, desktop only.
obs_note: Search for Topmind Stream in Obsidian community plugins, or add the repository above in BRAT.
obs_img_alt: Topmind Stream inside Obsidian: this week’s timeline
skl_what: A skill pack for hosts such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Hermes. The only daily entry is topmind, which routes to six actions: capture, organize, write, memory, maintain, and loop. Two optional connectors (WeRead and X) and optional bookkeeping are included.
skl_for: People who manage notes inside an agent and do not need the desktop app.
skl_note: The npm installer also installs shared/ and links the skills for several hosts.
pres_what: A skill for formal business decks (TopPPT HTML). Three shapes: a talk, a research report, or an architecture brief. Day to day you page through HTML; export an editable PPTX when the layout needs editing. Twelve styles, in light and dark themes.
pres_for: People preparing talks, research reports, or architecture briefs.
pres_note: Requires Node.js 18+ (used by the npx installer and for PPTX export). HTML uses only the Python standard library. The Release zip or git clone also work; see the README.
pres_sample_a_alt: Talk mode sample: a business-blue cover slide
pres_sample_b_alt: Research mode sample: a mckinsey-style cover slide
pres_sample_c_alt: Architecture mode sample: a graphite-dark cover slide
pp_meta_title: Topmind Presentation — HTML slides and an editable PPTX
pp_meta_description: Topmind Presentation builds formal business decks: a talk, a research report, or an architecture brief. Page through HTML, export an editable PPTX when needed, with twelve styles.
pp_lede: The skill is topmind-presentation, branded TopPPT HTML. HTML and PPTX come from one content model: you page through HTML day to day and export an editable PPTX when the layout needs editing.
pp_modes_lead: The three images below are the cover slides of the sample reports in the repository.
pp_mode_a_d: A deck for the stage, one claim per screen.
pp_mode_b_d: A research report with exhibits, sources, and takeaway bars.
pp_mode_c_d: An architecture brief built around topology, swimlane, and layered diagrams.
pp_styles_lead: Light for sharing, dark for a big screen. Below is the matrix of three modes across twelve styles.
pp_styles_alt: Topmind Presentation style matrix: talk, research, and architecture modes across twelve styles
pp_tool_title: Shortcuts that work as soon as it opens.
pp_tool_lead: Every delivered HTML file has a toolbar at the top. Here are its buttons and keys.
pp_tool_theme_d: Light for sharing, dark for a big screen. Remembered per file.
pp_tool_style_d: Switch among twelve styles live. Only the look changes, never the content.
pp_tool_pptx_d: Preview the page sequence and copy a prompt back into the chat to export.
pp_tool_help_d: Explains the two PPTX export routes and their dependencies.
pp_tool_full_d: Immersive presenting, with arrow keys to page.
pp_tool_fold_d: Folds into a mini bar. The position is remembered per file.
create_title: From draft to post, then to slides.
create_lead: Two separate repositories, installed separately. The writing skills produce articles, briefs, covers, and long images. The presentation skill turns content into a deck you can page through.
write_what: Seven writing, formatting and image skills behind one installer; install only what you need. X short posts verify first-hand sources, find the original post and images, then write and lay out; the body is one copy-ready plain-text block with sensible paragraphs and lists and no AI tone, while links, original images and generated images are sent separately; emoji are optional in short posts (TopMind system only) and never used in jokes; it asks before making any image.
write_for: Creators who write WeChat posts, X longform, briefs and short jokes, and need formatting, covers and long images.
write_note: Replace topmind-wechat-post with any skill name below.
write_img_alt: Topmind Writing Skills cover: WeChat posts, X longform, briefs, and covers
ws_wechat: WeChat long-form end to end: delivery pack, review and rewrite, three quality gates, inline WeChat layout, and a publish checklist.
ws_x: X longform: Markdown draft to one-click-copy HTML plus a plain-text fallback with emoji lists, a cover and a publish checklist.
ws_briefs: Briefs: one topic, explained. Sources → images → content → layout; no HTML by default — the X post is one copy-ready plain-text block, with links (source and publish time) and 1–2 original images sent separately, and the WeChat version as a separate Markdown block.
ws_viral: X jokes: 18 types plus hook × body × closer combinations, one sentence per line with blank lines between, no emoji at all, plain bullet lines; each post body is one copy-ready plain-text block, with links and images sent separately and internal tags listed apart; asks before making an image.
ws_cover: Covers: 22 styles, 12 title treatments and a background library, cropped for X longform, WeChat and 16:9 X short posts.
ws_poster: Long images: lay out in HTML, then render a 2x screenshot with headless Chrome for rankings, infographics, and posters.
ws_format: Formatter: turn existing text into duanzi or a short post. Layout only, words unchanged (fidelity check); short-post lists become 「·」/「1）」 or optional emoji bullets, duanzi drops all emoji; links and source lines are pulled out to send separately, leaving one copy-ready plain-text body.
ws_combo: brief → format; joke → format; brief without an original image → ask, then a 16:9 cover; longer than a post → X longform or WeChat long-form; data long image → poster.

about_title: A static page with no tracking.
about_lead: topmindspace.github.io introduces these five projects. GitHub Pages publishes it straight from the repository's main branch.
about_p1_d: HTML, CSS, and plain JavaScript, with no build step or framework. No web fonts, no analytics, no cookies.
about_p2_d: Switch language and theme at the top right. The theme follows your system until you pick one, and the choice stays in your browser. With Reduce Motion on, nothing animates.
about_p3_t: Releases are the source of truth
about_p3_d: Versions and descriptions are checked against each repository's latest Release and README. The check date is in the footer. If they differ, the repository wins.

ws_xrules: One shared contract for X short posts and jokes: verify sources and find the original post and images first, then write and lay out; the body is one copy-ready plain-text block (hashtags last), while links (including sources), original images and generated images are sent separately — one message for the body, one for links, one for images; emoji are optional in short posts (emoji or 「1）」/「·」 bullets) and never used in jokes; never - or 1.; X long-form and WeChat articles may keep in-text links. The linter blocks links, source lines and image notes in the body and flags AI-sounding phrases.

pp_dense_lead: From the 22-page city bus electrification review in the repository: dashboards, magazine pages and simple pages take turns, and a dense page is followed by a lighter one.

pp_simple_title: One number, one sentence or one icon makes a page.
pp_simple_lead: Simple pages come in 12 variants: number, statement, paragraph, icon and single chart, aligned left, centered or split. Four of them are shown below.
pp_simple_alt: Four simple pages: a large number, a centered statement, an icon with text, and a single chart with a readout
pp_beautify_title: New layouts, not a single word changed.
pp_beautify_lead: The original is read-only. Before the new deck is delivered, every word, number, chart value, image and speaker note is checked against the original. Slides with several charts become dashboards or paired charts, and table plus chart becomes a half-table page.
